output: {"answers":{"v02":"Precision and recall answer two different questions about the same search. Suppose a search for \"jaguar\" returns 10 results: 2 are about the animal, 8 are car pages; the database actually contains 5 animal pages, so 3 were missed. Precision asks: of what I retrieved, how much is right? 2/10 = 20%. Recall asks: of all relevant items that exist, how much did I find? 2/5 = 40%. The denominators differ — retrieved items vs. all relevant items — and that's the whole distinction. The two trade off: stricter filtering raises precision but loses recall. Which to prioritize depends on the cost of each error: a medical screening test should favor recall (missing a sick patient is worse than a false alarm), while a spam filter should favor precision (deleting a real email is worse than letting spam through).","v07":"公共物品有两个特征：不付钱也挡不住你用（非排他），多人同时用也不互相损耗（非竞争），比如路灯、防洪堤。搭便车由此产生：既然别人出钱建了路灯，我不出钱照样享受，理性的选择就是等着。麻烦在于人人都这样算，路灯就没人建——每个人的理性决定汇成一个对大家都差的结果。所以这类东西通常由税收出资，强制人人分摊。判断依据：一个物品若同时满足这两个特征，市场往往供给不足；一旦开始变拥挤，多用会妨碍别人（有了竞争性），收费就可行了，比如收费公园。注意边界：公路、电视广播这类只满足其中一条的东西，情况介于中间，不能一概而论。","v05":"信息熵衡量结果揭晓之前有多难猜：H = −Σ p·log p，输入一组概率，输出平均不确定性（单位常用比特）。均匀分布最不确定，是因为各结果机会均等时，你没有任何理由偏爱某一种猜测。极端情形看得最清楚：掷硬币，正面概率0.5时你每次都只能瞎猜，熵最大，为1比特；若正面概率是0.9，十次里有九次直接猜「正面」就对，熵明显更小；概率为1时必然发生，熵为0，毫无悬念。公式里的 −log p 表示小概率事件一旦发生带来的信息量大，再按概率加权取平均。准确的说法是：在取值个数固定的所有分布中，均匀分布的熵最大；分布越偏向某些结果，熵越小。所以「均匀更不确定」是有前提的结论，不是对任意两个分布都成立。","d07":"相关只说明两个量同涨同跌，因果才说明改变一个会带来另一个，两者经常被混在一起。例子：冰淇淋销量与溺水人数年年同步上升，但不是冰淇淋导致溺水，背后有共同原因——夏天高温让两件事都变多。看到相关时，可能是X导致Y、Y导致X、有第三个变量Z同时推动两者，也可能纯属巧合。区分的办法是控制混杂因素或随机对照：把人随机分成服药组和对照组，其他条件就对齐了，剩下的差异才能归给药。日常判断可以问两个问题：有没有第三个变量能同时解释两者？这个结论是观察得来的，还是做过随机对照？没做对照，就只说相关，别下因果结论。","d04":"Opportunity cost is the value of the best option you give up, not the sum of everything you pass on. A free afternoon, three options: tutoring for $50, a gym session, or a nap. If you choose the nap, the cost is not zero just because no money changed hands — it's the $50 of tutoring, assuming that was your next-best option. The gym doesn't add to the cost; only the single highest-valued forgone alternative counts. This is the beginner's decision rule: measure a choice against the next-best alternative, never against \"nothing.\" Time is the budget here, so a cost exists even without spending money. One caveat: this presumes you actually ranked the options — if you genuinely value the nap most, the opportunity cost of napping is, by your own scale, lower than tutoring's value.","v04":"An operation is idempotent if calling it once and calling it many times leave the same final state. Setting a user's status to \"inactive\" is idempotent; adding 1 to a counter is not, because each call changes the result. Distributed systems care because requests can time out even after the server processed them — the client doesn't know if the server saw the message, so it retries. Without idempotency, a retried \"charge $10 to order 42\" double-charges the customer. The standard fix is an idempotency key: the client attaches a unique key to the request, and the server remembers which keys it has already handled, returning the stored result instead of repeating the effect. A practical design rule: prefer operations phrased as \"set the value to X\" over \"add X\" when retries are possible.","d05":"检测出阳性，真正患病的概率往往远低于「准确率」，贝叶斯公式算的就是这个数。设某病患病率是千分之一，检测灵敏度99%（患者99%呈阳性），假阳率5%。想象10000人：患者约10人，其中约9.9人阳性；健康9990人，按5%约有500人也呈阳性。阳性人群共约510人，真正的患者只占约10/510≈2%。贝叶斯公式 P(患病|阳性) = P(阳性|患病)×P(患病) / P(阳性) 做的就是这件事，分母是把「患者测出阳性」和「健康人误报阳性」两条路加起来。关键在方向：P(阳性|患病)是检测本身的性能，P(患病|阳性)才是你要的答案，两者方向相反。患病率越低，同一个阳性越可能是假警报；所以初检阳性后复查一次，第一次结果更新了先验，患病概率会大幅上升。","d06":"A cache keeps a copy of data close by so reads are fast; invalidation is deciding when that copy is too old and must be thrown away or refreshed. Example: a product page is cached for an hour. The store updates the price, but users keep seeing the old price until the cached copy expires or is removed — that stale window is the core problem. Common strategies: a TTL (expire after a fixed time — simple, but data is stale until then); delete-on-write (when the price updates, delete the cached entry so the next read fetches fresh data); or event-based invalidation (the update publishes a message and every cache that hears it drops its copy). The hard part is that with many caches across services, guaranteeing every copy reflects the truth gets genuinely complicated — hence the saying that cache invalidation is one of the hard problems in computer science. Your freshness requirement picks the strategy.","v08":"Little's law connects three averages in any waiting system: L = λW, where L is the average number of items in the system, λ the arrival rate, and W the average time each spends there (waiting plus service). Barber shop example: customers arrive every 10 minutes, so λ = 6 per hour; each spends about 30 minutes in the shop. Then L = 6 × 0.5 = 3 people inside on average — no need to count them. The law is useful precisely because L is often hard to measure while λ and W are easy, and it works both directions: given any two, you get the third. Watch the conditions: it holds in steady state (rates stable, queue not exploding), for long-run averages, and with consistent units (per hour with hours). If arrivals double and capacity doesn't, W must grow — the law tells you where the pressure shows up.","v06":"A deadlock is when processes hold resources and wait for each other's, so none can ever proceed. Example: process A holds lock 1 and now requests lock 2; process B holds lock 2 and requests lock 1. Each blocks waiting for the other; neither releases what it holds, so both freeze forever — with no error message, which is what makes deadlocks nasty. Four conditions must all hold simultaneously: mutual exclusion (resources can't be shared), hold-and-wait (a process keeps its resources while waiting), no preemption (resources can't be forcibly taken), and circular wait (a ring of waiting processes). That's the diagnostic value: break any one condition and deadlock becomes impossible. The most common fix in practice is imposing a global lock ordering — every process acquires lock 1 before lock 2, which destroys the circle.","d02":"An average tells you where the center is, not how spread out the data is. Two classes can both average 70: one with scores between 69 and 71, another ranging from 30 to 100. Variance measures that spread — it is the average of squared distances from the mean. Steps: subtract the mean from each value, square the result, then average those squares. For {2, 4, 6}, the mean is 4; deviations are −2, 0, 2; squares are 4, 0, 4; the variance is (4+0+4)/3 ≈ 2.67. Squaring serves two purposes: deviations above and below the mean would cancel to exactly zero if merely summed, and squaring makes large deviations count much more than small ones. Its units are the square of the original units, so the square root (standard deviation) is reported when you want spread in the data's own units. Population variance divides by N because it assumes you have every member of the group.","v03":"自然选择改变种群的方式是筛选已有的变异，不是生物主动努力的结果。以羚羊为例：一代羚羊出生时速度就有随机差异，这个差异是可遗传的。跑得慢的更容易被狮子抓住，留下的后代少；跑得快的后代多，于是下一代种群里「快」相关的基因比例升高。关键的区分在两处：变异是随机的，但筛选不是——环境决定哪些个体留下更多后代；被改变的是种群的平均性状，个体终其一生不会因此改变。长颈鹿「伸脖子够树叶所以脖子变长」是错误图景，那是把个体后天的用劲当成了遗传，事实上只有出生时就带着更长脖子的个体被留下得更多。这个机制成立的条件：变异可遗传、变异影响繁殖成功、环境持续筛选。满足这些条件，种群性状就会逐代移动。","d03":"正反馈指输出的结果反过来加强输入，让变化像滚雪球一样越滚越大。话筒对准音箱就是最直观的例子：一点微小的杂音被放大，放大的声音又进入话筒，再被放大，几秒内变成刺耳的啸叫。这个结构在很多地方出现：存款利息并入本金，下期的利息按更大的本金计算，财富指数增长；信谣言的人越多，传得越快，传播范围加速扩大。放大本身没有好坏，正负描述的是方向——放大变化还是抵消变化——好坏取决于被放大的是什么。抢购推高涨价预期、涨价预期再推高抢购，放大的是泡沫；电路啸叫放大噪音，直到设备烧毁。而且放大不可能无限持续，本金、市场容量、音箱功率都会设上限。与之相对的负反馈把偏差拉回原位，才是稳定的来源。分析系统时先找回路方向，再问它放大的是什么。","d08":"Compound growth means gains themselves start earning gains, so growth multiplies rather than adds. Take $1000 at 10% per year: simple interest adds $100 every year, giving $1300 after three years. Compounding instead folds each year's interest into the principal: year 2 earns $110, year 3 earns $121, ending at $1331. The gap widens with time — after 30 years, simple gives $4000 while compounding gives about $17,450. A handy check is the rule of 72: money doubles in roughly 72 divided by the annual rate. The starting amount matters because growth is multiplication: $2000 at the same rate ends at exactly double the $1000 outcome, and money that starts earlier compounds for more years. Time and base work together — the same rate applied to a larger, earlier base pulls far ahead. Real investments don't guarantee rates, so treat this as the structure of growth, not a promise.","d01":"似然回答的问题是：假设某个假设为真，看到手头这批数据的概率有多大。方向和高中概率题正好相反：概率题是固定假设算数据——已知硬币均匀（正面概率0.5），抛10次出7次正面的概率约为0.117；似然是数据已经确定，反过来给不同的假设打分——10次7正这个数据摆在眼前，若正面概率真是0.5，出现这数据的可能性约0.117；若是0.7，可能性约0.266。后者似然更大，说明「0.7」与数据更相容。注意似然不是「假设为真的概率」，它是「数据在假设之下的概率」。后验概率才是前者：由贝叶斯公式把似然乘上先验、再归一，得到「看到数据后假设为真的概率」。似然是桥，后验是终点；而且似然大只说明假设与数据相容，不等于该假设为真——小概率事件也会发生。","v01":"过拟合是模型把训练数据里的细节和噪音也当成了规律，导致在新数据上表现变差。打个比方：一个学生把历年考题的答案一字不差背下来，原题考满分，题目稍一变化就不及格——他记住的是「这份卷子」，不是解题方法。判断依据看落差：训练数据上准确率很高，换一批新数据准确率明显下降，这个差距就是过拟合的信号。发生的原因通常是模型太复杂、训练数据太少，或者训练轮数太多，模型把数据中的偶然波动也拟合了进去。常见对策：增加数据量、换更简单的模型、加正则化约束、提前停止训练。这个概念不限于机器学习——好的规律应当概括一类情况，而不是复述已经见过的样本；判断任何方法好不好，都要看它对没见过的情况行不行。"}
